summary: Full auth verification for CUGO App (JWT + httpOnly cookies). Backend: 10/10 pytest cases pass in /app/backend/tests/test_auth.py covering login success/failure, /me with/without cookie, refresh rotation, refresh without cookie, logout invalidation, unknown user, inactive user (via psql toggle, restored), bcrypt hash format ($2b$), and cookie HttpOnly flag. Response bodies verified free of hashed_password/password/access_token/refresh_token. Frontend (Playwright, headed preview URL): / unauthenticated -> /login; wrong password shows login-error 'Invalid email or password'; correct login -> dashboard-root visible with user-email 'admin@cugo.app' and user-role 'Super Admin'; page reload keeps session (via /auth/me); logout -> /login and / stays on /login; localStorage & sessionStorage empty throughout; document.cookie is empty in JS confirming access_token & refresh_token are httpOnly.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py refresh: exception handlers use bare `raise HTTPException` inside `except`; consider `raise ... from None` to suppress noisy chained tracebacks in logs.
seed.py updates password hash whenever ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env changes on restart (idempotent + rotates hash) — matches playbook requirement.
Cookies set with SameSite=None + Secure via settings.COOKIE_SAMESITE / COOKIE_SECURE — verified working over the HTTPS preview.
No brute-force lockout implemented yet (playbook mentions 5-fail lockout as a nice-to-have). Out of scope per problem statement (core endpoints only), but note for a future hardening iteration.
JWT is stateless with no server-side blacklist — after logout the cookie is cleared but a copied token would remain valid until expiry. Documented as accepted design in problem statement.
seed_data_creation: None — used seeded super_admin. Inactive-user test toggled is_active via psql and restored to true in a finally block.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Auth is green end-to-end. test_auth.py can serve as regression. Next iterations (branches CRUD, admin-created users, RBAC) can build on the fixture pattern here — a `logged_in_session` fixture can be extracted when needed.
